full_judgment: 38. It may be mentioned that the same principle has been followed by a preponderance of judicial opinion in this subcontinent in holding that even if in a decree for specific performance of contract for sale of a certain property there is no specific direction for delivery of possession of the said property, the said decree may be executed for the purpose of enforcing, delivery of possession of the said property to the decree-holder under the above quoted Rule 32(5) of Order 21, C.P.C., on the basis that delivery of possession of the property was an implied term of the contract and also an implied term of the decree for specific performance of the said contract. Reference may be made to the cases of Atal Behary Vs. Barada Prasad, A.I.R. 1931 Patna 179, Kartic Chandra Vs. Dibakar, A.I.R. 1952 Cal. 363, Arkin Vs. Sahu A.I.R. 1950 Allahabad 415, Janardhan Vs. Girtlhari A.I.R. 1957 Patna 701, Warn. Vs. Chaudhury A.I.R. 1949 Lahore 72, Dudulal Vs. De Khmer A.I.R. 1963 M.P. 86 and Birgis Jahau Vs. Muhammad Hasan (1963) 15 DLR 298 PLD 1964 Dacca 202, in which it has been held that the executing Court has abundant authority to execute a decree for specific performance of contract for sale of a property for enforcing delivery of possession of the said property, even though the decree under execution is silent as to the relief of delivery of possession. In our view a decree for specific performance of a contract for, sale of a property has been correctly interpreted in the said decisions.
